newsitem.title: USA: World Bank assessing carbon pollution's costs.
newsitem.headline: World Bank assessing carbon pollution's costs.

text.p: The World Bank will release a study this summer on how factoring in costs of environmental damage from fossil fuels would have influenced the design of its projects, officials said Tuesday.
"The study should help clarify how climate change concerns could influence the Bank's lending, provide support for policy formulation and identify priority investments," the bank said in a statement.

At a briefing, officials of the bank's Environment Department said the study should indicate how projects might have been shifted from reliance on coal and oil to more environmentally benign technologies if what they termed "shadow costs" had been factored in.
The bank is doing its study as the Clinton administration is preparing an analysis of the economic effects of reducing emissions of heat-trapping carbon pollution from fossil fuels.
The administration has said it will use its analysis to determine the amount of emissions reductions it should press for in international negotiations on reducing climate-changing pollution.

With the talks set to end in December, industrialized countries so far are discussing setting pollution caps for themselves while urging developing countries -- the bank's clients -- to join in programs to curb pollution.
